comparison: Sparse (Jaccard bag-of-words) vs dense (UniXcoder) retriever, same RepoCoder pipeline: Table 2(a) vs Appendix B Table 6(a), RepoEval line completion, iteration 1 (single-pass RAG). Other comparisons in the paper (In-File vs RAG; Iter-1 vs Iter-2; Oracle) add context from zero or add extra model calls.
model_config: Same generator per arm (GPT-3.5-Turbo; also CodeGen-Mono 350M/2B/6B); same prompt template and hyper-parameters (Sec 4.2); only the retriever differs.
dataset_metric: RepoEval line completion (1,600 samples), Exact Match / Edit Similarity (%)
budget_control: Explicit cap applied the same way to both arms: 'The length of retrieved code snippets is set to half the prompt length' (prompt+output max 4,096 tokens for GPT-3.5, 2,048 for CodeGen), K=10 snippets max, window Sw=20/Ss=10. Realized token counts per arm not reported.
arm_a: Top-K (<=10) 20-line sliding-window snippets ranked by Jaccard similarity, prepended to in-file context
arm_b: Top-K (<=10) 20-line sliding-window snippets ranked by UniXcoder cosine similarity, prepended to in-file context
other_changes: None reported beyond the retriever. Both arms make one retrieval and one generation call at iteration 1.
delta: GPT-3.5-Turbo line EM at iteration 1: 55.31 (sparse) vs 54.56 (dense), -0.75 pp. At iteration 2: 56.81 vs 56.25.
rationale: Only the retriever changes, and both arms use the same snippet count, window size and token cap: 'the simple sparse retriever achieves equivalent performance'. The cap is equal, but realized lengths are not reported. Both arms are flat-text retrieval, so the comparison does not test a structured representation.

comparison: Retriever comparison, Table 4: BM25 vs UniXCoder vs OpenAI ada embeddings for cross-file context (Sec 3.5 / retrieval benchmark paragraph).
model_config: Same code LM per row group (CodeGen25-7B; StarCoder-15.5B), greedy decoding; only the retriever differs.
dataset_metric: CrossCodeEval (Python/Java/TypeScript/C#), code-match Exact Match / Edit Similarity
budget_control: Equal cap across arms: top-5 retrieved 10-line chunks, 'We consider a maximum of 512 BPE tokens for such context, and the rest of the tokens will be truncated.' Realized per-arm token counts not reported.
arm_a: Top-5 cross-file chunks retrieved by BM25 (lexical)
arm_b: Top-5 cross-file chunks retrieved by UniXCoder or OpenAI text-embedding-ada-002 cosine similarity
other_changes: None beyond the retriever (embedding max length differs inside the retriever only: 256 for UniXCoder, 8,000 for ada).
delta: StarCoder-15.5B Python EM: 15.72 (BM25) vs 15.87 (UniXCoder) vs 16.47 (ada). The cited 8.82 -> 15.72 change is no-context vs retrieval, which also changes the budget from 0 to 512 tokens.
rationale: Same model, same top-5 chunks and 512-token truncation, and only the retriever varies: 'we perform experiments with different retrievers from sparse (BM25 ...) to neural'. The record's headline no-context vs retrieval comparison is not budget-matched.

comparison: Knowledge-source ablation without evolution, Table 4 (single-pass retrieval; Doc only vs Code+Doc vs Exec+Code+Doc), with realized tokens from Table 7 (DocPrompting = Doc only, no evolution; RK = knowledge soup, no evolution). The Fig. 3 token-threshold sweep (EvoR vs DocPrompting at equal total tokens) changes the iterative loop, number of calls and knowledge sources at once.
model_config: Same generator per arm (ChatGPT or CodeLlama); INSTRUCTOR-xl retriever; max context 4,096 for all settings (Sec 3.2).
dataset_metric: EvoR-Bench (Scipy-M, Tensor-M, Ring, Pony), average execution accuracy (%)
budget_control: Nominal cap of 4,096 context tokens for every arm, with code snippets capped at 300 and documentation filling the rest (Appendix F). Realized tokens differ (Table 7, ChatGPT avg): DocPrompting 3,751 vs RK 4,716 tokens per example.
arm_b: Retrieved knowledge soup: execution feedback + code snippets + documentation
other_changes: Table 7 RK also formulates the query as LLM-explained code ('Single-time') rather than the raw question, which adds a ChatGPT explanation step. Table 4 rows are otherwise the same pipeline.
delta: ChatGPT avg execution accuracy: Doc 19.2 vs Exec+Code+Doc 22.4 (+3.2 pp) without evolution (Table 4). Tokens 3,751 vs 4,716 (Table 7). The paper notes 'around 25% more processed tokens'.
rationale: The arms share a 4,096 nominal cap, but realized tokens differ in the richer arm's favour: 'This enhancement is at the expense of around 25% more processed tokens for both models.' The headline EVOR vs DocPrompting comparison (35.3 vs 19.2, about 16k vs 3.7k tokens) is multi-change.

comparison: '+ R2C2-Enhance' vs '+ R2C2-Enhance w.o. Abs.' at inference without fine-tuning, Table 2 (R2C2-Bench); same contrast in Tables 3/4. The Table 5 ablation removes abstract context 'at the fine-tuning and the inference stages simultaneously', so its arms are differently trained models.
model_config: Same base model per arm (StarCoder-7B / Code Llama-7B / DeepSeekCoder-6.7B), no fine-tuning, same Jaccard retrieval with P=5/S=5.
budget_control: Explicit equal token cap: candidates are concatenated 'until the cumulative length, including the in-file context, reaches the maximum token limit of N=4096' for both arms. Abstract contexts (K=3) take part of the same budget. Realized lengths not reported separately.
arm_a: In-file context + top-3 abstract contexts (tree-sitter-extracted declarations/signatures) + snippet contexts up to N=4,096
arm_b: In-file context + snippet contexts only (abstracts removed from the candidate pool), up to N=4,096
other_changes: None at inference. The Table 5 variant also differs in fine-tuning.
delta: StarCoder-7B average EM 24.8 vs 24.3 (+0.5 pp); DeepSeekCoder-6.7B 30.1 vs 29.5; Code Llama-7B 19.9 vs 19.7 (Table 2). The record's 31.2 vs 42.1 is Table 5, which compares a no-snippet model against the full model, both fine-tuned.
rationale: Both arms fill the same prompt cap, and only the composition of the candidate pool changes: 'we report results without using abstract contexts in the candidate retrieval pool.' The record's Table 5 claim is weaker than stated because those arms are separately fine-tuned.
graph_class_check: n/a (primary repr is hybrid). AST-derived abstract context is compared under the shared N=4,096 cap (Table 2); realized per-arm lengths are not reported.

comparison: Prompting-phase static-analysis context (Prompt-F file-level imports / Prompt-T token-level valid names) vs RAG (RepoCoder, 1 iteration) as the only cross-file context, RQ3 Figure 4.
model_config: Same code LLM per comparison (DeepSeek-Coder-6.7B, StarCoderBase-7B, CodeLlama-7B), greedy decoding, max_new_tokens 64.
budget_control: Nominal cap only: in-file truncated to 2,000 tokens and 'each cross-file context to 3,000 tokens'. RAG uses 3 snippets of 20 lines. Realized token counts per arm not reported, and the authors note that file-level dependencies contain a 'larger scale of context' than the token-level list.
arm_a: Prompt-F: imported cross-file code via static analysis (tree-sitter/ast + Jedi/JDT), or Prompt-T: list of valid method/variable names
other_changes: None in prompting-phase comparisons. Decoding and post-processing strategies change decoding or add beam search.
delta: Only 'higher than RAG on most of the studied models' (Figure 4 is an image; values not stated in the text). Prompt-F vs in-file: Python Line EM 27.80 vs 9.02 (+18.78) for DeepSeek-Coder-6.7B, which also adds context.
rationale: Only the context source changes, but the realized amount is uncontrolled: '[prompting-phase integration] actually includes more contexts into the input' and file-level dependencies carry a 'larger scale of context'.

comparison: Retrieval-technique ablation inside RAMBO, Table 4 (Lexical BPE+Jaccard vs Semantic UniXCoder vs Hybrid). RAMBO vs RepoCoder (Tables 2-3) changes the whole pipeline.
model_config: Same DeepSeek Coder 6.7B and same RAMBO pipeline (sketch -> EEI -> RUE -> generation) for every arm.
dataset_metric: RAMBO benchmark (Java MBC), CodeBLEU / Compilation Rate / EM
budget_control: Not reported: 'The number of snippets included in the prompt is optimized based on the available prompt length'. No token limit or realized length is given.
arm_a: Usages/similar methods ranked by lexical (BPE Jaccard) similarity
arm_b: Same candidates ranked by semantic (UniXCoder cosine) similarity
delta: CodeBLEU 53.20 vs 52.61; EM 18.94% vs 18.09% (lexical vs semantic).
rationale: Only the similarity function changes, but no budget is reported ('optimized based on the available prompt length'). The conservative rule treats an unreported budget as not budget-matched.

comparison: Knowledge ablation, Table 4: PE (empty knowledge base) vs K1Trans (+dependency usage examples) vs K2Trans (+target-language code samples) vs K3Trans (+translation pairs).
model_config: Same Claude-3.5-Sonnet, same prompt format and pipeline (including self-debugging) for every arm.
budget_control: Not controlled: each arm adds knowledge to the prompt. No token counts reported.
arm_a: PE prompt: instructions + repository-context source function, no retrieved knowledge
arm_b: Same prompt + retrieved dependency usage examples (K1), + code samples (K2), + translation pairs (K3)
other_changes: None beyond the added knowledge. Table 6 also varies knowledge-base maturity.
rationale: Arms differ only in which knowledge is added, and context grows with each addition: 'by progressively reducing the provided knowledge categories'. No budget is held or reported.

comparison: Working-memory ablation, Sec 4.3.1 / Figure 7: full Prometheus vs Prometheus without working memory, on 50 random SWE-bench Verified instances.
model_config: Same GPT-5 (temperature 1.0), same prompts and agents: 'keeping all other components, model backbones, prompts, and execution settings unchanged'.
dataset_metric: SWE-bench Verified (50-instance random subset), resolution rate; total inference cost (USD)
budget_control: Not equalized, but realized cost is reported and the mechanism arm is smaller: $200.79 with memory vs $367.73 without memory across 50 issues. Costs are in dollars, not context tokens; per-call context size and number of calls are not reported.
arm_a: Knowledge-graph context engine with working memory: retrieved context units are cached and reused by sub-query (memory-first protocol)
arm_b: Same knowledge-graph context engine without working memory: context is re-retrieved on each query
other_changes: None by design. The number of retrieval steps and LLM calls inside the loop changes as a result (not reported). Single run, n=50.
delta: Resolution 70.00% vs 56.00% (+14 pp absolute; reported as '+25.0%' relative). Cost $200.79 vs $367.73 (-45.4%).
rationale: Only the context-reuse mechanism changes, and the mechanism arm costs less: 'reducing inference cost by approximately 45.4% while simultaneously improving the issue resolution rate'. Caveats: cost is in USD rather than context tokens, n=50, single run, and the knowledge graph is present in both arms, so this does not test the graph.
graph_class_check: n/a (primary repr is hybrid). The knowledge-graph/AST representation itself is never ablated. RQ1/RQ2 compare against other agents (multi-change).

comparison: Function Chunking RAG (code parsed into function-level chunks) vs Sliding Window RAG (500-line windows), Table 3 with token usage from Table 8. The v2 paper has no separate 'AST-based retrieval' arm; function chunking is the structure-aware arm.
model_config: Same LLM per pair (e.g. Kimi K2, GPT-5.1, Qwen3-Coder); same voyage-code-3 embeddings and Top-K=10 for both RAG variants.
budget_control: Realized input tokens reported (Table 8): Function Chunking 3,042 vs Sliding Window 6,302 input tokens per question. The structured arm is smaller (identical figures listed for every model).
other_changes: None. Agent arms (SWE-agent/OpenHands) change the scaffold and use about 100x tokens.
delta: Kimi K2: 60.08 (function chunking) vs 62.44 (sliding window); GPT-5.1: 66.57 vs 66.79; Qwen3-Coder-30B: 63.40 vs 64.86. Input tokens 3,042 vs 6,302.
rationale: Same model, same K and embedding; the structure-aware arm is not larger ('Function Chunking RAG | 3,042' vs 'Sliding Window RAG | 6,302' input tokens) and scores slightly lower. The record's headline (Direct -> RAG -> agent) is multi-change and unmatched.

comparison: Component ablation, Table 3 (DevEval, DeepSeek-V3): full InlineCoder vs w/o upstream (call-graph caller context) and vs w/o inline (callee/usage context not inlined). Baseline comparisons (Tables 1-2) change the whole method.
model_config: Same DeepSeek-V3 backbone, temperature 0, same draft + confidence pipeline for every ablation arm.
budget_control: Not controlled or reported: models use 'their native context window size' (128K / 262,144 / 400K input limits). No realized token counts are given for any arm.
arm_a: Full: draft + upstream callers + inlined usage context + downstream callees (call graph via tree-sitter/Pydepcall) + confidence statement
arm_b: Same minus upstream caller context (w/o upstream) or minus usage-context inlining (w/o inline)
delta: EM 11.56 vs 9.48 (w/o upstream, -2.12) and vs 9.15 (w/o inline, -2.41); BLEU 57.12 vs 51.34 / 52.35.
rationale: Each ablation removes one context component under the same model and pipeline, but no budget is held or reported ('We configured each model to its native context window size').
graph_class_check: Primary repr is call_dep_graph. No budget-matched comparison of the call-graph representation exists in the paper: no arm reports realized tokens, and the RAG/DRACO/GraphCoder baselines differ in the whole pipeline.

comparison: Ablation 'w/o DC' (dependency-context snippets removed from the retrieval codebase) vs full AlignCoder, Table III. 'w/o RL' changes retriever training and 'w/o QH' removes the sampler calls.
model_config: DeepSeekCoder-7B generator for every ablation arm; same RL-trained retriever and query enhancement.
dataset_metric: CrossCodeEval Python/Java, RepoEval line/API; EM / ES
budget_control: Not reported: no number of retrieved snippets, token cap or realized length is stated for any arm or baseline.
arm_a: Codebase of base (Split-Aggregate) snippets + dependency-context snippets
delta: CrossCodeEval Python EM 33.92 vs 31.44 (-7.3% relative); Java 28.28 vs 27.44.
rationale: Only the retrievable representation changes ('w/o DC indicates that the dependency context is not considered'), but the retrieval budget is never reported. The headline vs RLCoder/RepoCoder comparison is multi-change (trained retriever, sampler calls).

comparison: SWEzze (AST-segment learned compressor) vs LLMLingua-2 (token-level compressor), and vs No_compression, inside the same Agentless pipeline: Table 2 (resolution) with Table 3 (realized prompt tokens).
model_config: Same downstream repair LLM per comparison (DeepSeek-V3.2, Qwen3-Coder-Next, GPT-5.2), same Agentless localization and context.
budget_control: Realized prompt tokens reported (Table 3). SWEzze is smaller than LLMLingua-2 on all three models (8,658 vs 11,480; 2,922 vs 4,408; 4,492 vs 7,237) and smaller than No_compression (21,808 / 9,457 / 16,893). The nominal targets differ (5x for SWEzze, defaults for baselines). LongCodeZip uses fewer tokens than SWEzze on Qwen and GPT-5.2.
arm_a: Agentless context pruned at AST-derived segment granularity by a cross-encoder trained on oracle-distilled minimal contexts
arm_b: Same Agentless context compressed token-by-token by LLMLingua-2 (or left uncompressed)
other_changes: Only the compressor step differs. Each compressor is a separately trained model, but the repair LLM and pipeline are fixed.
delta: Resolution rate SWEzze vs LLMLingua-2: 0.522 vs 0.490 (DeepSeek-V3.2), 0.420 vs 0.386 (Qwen3-Coder-Next), 0.578 vs 0.544 (GPT-5.2). Vs No_compression: +4.4 / +2.0 / +4.6 pp.
rationale: Same repair model and pipeline, and the structure-aware arm uses fewer realized prompt tokens yet resolves more ('SWEzze achieves the best issue resolution performance across all three LLMs'). Against LongCodeZip the budgets cross over, so that comparison is not matched.
graph_class_check: Primary repr is ast. Yes, budget-matched comparisons exist: the AST-segment compressor uses fewer realized prompt tokens than LLMLingua-2 and No_compression (Table 3) and scores higher (Table 2). Note that AST is the pruning unit; the model sees pruned source code, not an AST serialization.

comparison: Baseline agent with native repo tools vs same agent + CAIS retrieval tool, two case studies (Tables 1, 3, 4).
model_config: Same agent (Claude Code v2.1.154, Sonnet 4.6) and prompts; CAIS is added as an extra tool.
dataset_metric: Two proprietary SDK documentation case studies; retained findings count (qualitative, author-filtered); input tokens, wall-clock time over 5 runs
budget_control: Not held, but realized input tokens are reported and the CAIS arm is lower: 17.4K vs 14.6K (case 1), 112.3K vs 76.8K (case 2).
arm_a: Agent with file reads, keyword search, symbol navigation
arm_b: Same tools + CAIS hybrid BM25 + dense (DRAMA) retrieval over an indexed SDK corpus
other_changes: Agent tool set/scaffold differs (an extra retrieval tool), and the number of LLM calls rises sharply: 2.4 vs 17.6 (case 1), 17.4 vs 30.2 (case 2). In case 2 CAIS is used in a post-generation review.
delta: Retained findings 5 (baseline) vs 13 (+CAIS). Input tokens -16% / -32%. Wall-clock -22% / -34%.
rationale: The arms differ in tool scaffold and in the number of model calls ('LLM calls went up because the agent issued retrieval queries as tool calls'). The quality outcome is an author-filtered qualitative findings count from two case studies.

comparison: Agent4cs vs HR-CS (and CS-BF) baselines, Table 2 (function-level) and Table 3 (hierarchical). Direct vs AST-enhanced prompting is described (Fig. 4) but not reported as a separate quantitative ablation.
model_config: Same backbone per row (7 LLMs: GPT-4o, GPT-4.1, GPT-5, Gemini-2.5-flash, LLaMA-3.1-8B, Qwen3-8B, Gemma3-4B), but different agent pipelines.
dataset_metric: CodeSearchNet/CodeXGLUE repository subsets; Rouge-L, BLEU-1, BERTScore, SentenceBERT, LLM-judge; keyword coverage and semantic similarity across folder layers
budget_control: Not reported: no token counts. Summary lengths vary by model (Figure 9).
arm_a: Agent4cs: summarization agent + QA-feedback agent (function level); bottom-up layer-wise summaries with a keyword-extraction agent
arm_b: HR-CS: single-pass AST-enhanced prompting with package-level aggregation (CS-BF: function-class-repository scheme with few-shot)
other_changes: Number of agents and LLM calls (iterative QA feedback loop), prompts and hierarchy scheme all differ.
delta: GPT-4o function-level Rouge-L 0.189 vs 0.177 (HR-CS). Hierarchical keyword coverage GPT-4o 0.682 -> 0.829. Semantic similarity +8% average.
rationale: Full multi-agent pipeline vs a single-pass baseline ('Agent4cs comprises two collaborative agents: a code summarization agent and a quality assurance agent'), so representation, loop and call count change together.

comparison: With-image vs no-image ablation, Table 3, same system and model. (+VCE in Table 4 adds a separate VLM extraction stage.)
model_config: Same system/model per pair (e.g. MM-IssueLoc-VL-Embed-2B retriever; AgentLess/OpenHands with GPT-5.2 or Claude-Sonnet-4.6).
budget_control: Not reported: no token counts. Image inputs add tokens; at most two images per issue for the retriever.
arm_a: Issue text + attached images (up to two for the retriever)
other_changes: None. The comparison concerns issue-report modality, not repository-context representation.
delta: MM-IssueLoc-VL-Embed-2B File@5 32.06 (with image) vs 27.15 (no image), +4.91. AgentLess GPT-5.2 29.59 vs 26.93.
rationale: Same system and model with only the input modality changed, but the context amount is not controlled or reported: the no-image condition simply 'removes images'. Cross-system comparisons (agents vs retrievers) are multi-change.

comparison: Ablation of the structure-aware API-call selection signal: MRCoder vs w/o_API, Tables 3-4. MRCoder vs RAG/LongCodeZip (Tables 1-2) adds a draft model, Map-phase draft calls and parallel decoding.
model_config: Same target/draft model pairs (Qwen2.5-Coder-7B/1.5B; DeepSeek-Coder-6.7B/1.3B), same BM25 top-K, same Map-Reduce pipeline.
dataset_metric: CoderEval and DevEval, Pass@1; context tokens (GPT tokenizer)
budget_control: Realized context tokens reported (Table 4) and the structured arm is larger: e.g. Qwen CoderEval K=10 3.6k (MRCoder) vs 2.1k (w/o_API); DeepSeek 3.5k vs 2.0k.
arm_a: Context selected by tree-sitter API-call matching between drafts and candidates + BM25 draft similarity
arm_b: Context selected by BM25 draft similarity only (API-call signal removed)
other_changes: None beyond the removed selection signal.
delta: DevEval Pass@1 Qwen K=3: 19.9 vs 14.8 (-5.1). CoderEval DeepSeek K=10: 36.5 vs 36.0. Tokens about 40-50% higher with the API signal.
rationale: Only the selection signal changes, but the structured arm keeps more context: 'Removing the API or similarity modules consistently reduces token consumption'. MRCoder vs RAG uses fewer tokens but adds draft-model calls and parallel decoding, so it is multi-change.
